RESULTS: P1.1 INCONCLUSIVE (data-dependent, no such contact string in current dataset), P1.3 AFP signature persistence PASS, P1.4 RAMS resume from drafts FAIL (all distinctive fields render blank after Resume), P1.5 Subbie Payment Certificate Resume PASS (GenericToolPage hydrated all 4 fields), Finance Hub vs Payment Tracker PASS (numbers match — both £0.00, no mismatch).

ui_bugs.issue: RAMS Resume from /app/drafts navigates to /app/rams?draft=<id> but the form renders with EVERY distinctive field blank. Reproduced: filled clientName='QA RAMS Client Ltd', principalContractor='QA Morris Contractors', siteAddress='Unit 4, 7 Verification Lane, London EC1A 1AA', supervisorName='QA Sam Foreman', task='QA hydration test — fit fire dampers L3-B7' → tool-save-draft-btn → /app/drafts → click Resume → landed on /app/rams. Actual input values captured post-restore: {rams-client:'', rams-pc:'', rams-site:'', rams-supervisor:'', rams-task:''}. No 'Draft restored' toast fired. Very likely a Rams.jsx mount-effect race: the useEffect at Rams.jsx:275 has [] deps and reads draftIdFromQuery() ONCE — if either (a) the draft is being persisted under a toolId that isn't 'rams' (DraftSaveButton normalises tool.id?) so the guard `d.toolId !== TOOL_ID` bails out silently, OR (b) the Resume link routes through /app/tool/rams first and the query param is not preserved through RedirectTo before Rams.jsx mounts, the hydration never runs. Recommend: (i) console.log the response of GET /api/drafts/<id> and the value of TOOL_ID compared to d.toolId in the effect, (ii) verify the Resume link target URL in the drafts list, and (iii) confirm draftIdFromQuery() actually returns the id at Rams mount time.

action_items: P1.4 (RAMS Resume) is broken end-to-end from the drafts list. Debug the mount-effect at Rams.jsx:275 — either the draft's toolId mismatches TOOL_ID='rams' (check DraftSaveButton.jsx serialisation), the Resume link routes via /app/tool/rams and the ?draft=<id> is lost through the RedirectTo, or draftIdFromQuery() runs before window.location.search is populated. Add a console.warn for each early-return in that useEffect during dev and re-run the flow.

P1.1 (AFP Riverside client mapping) could not be reproduced because the current admin dataset has clientContact=null and poNumber=null on the Riverside project. If the concern is real, seed a Job with clientContact='Sarah Mitchell — 07700 912846' and verify afp-clientName does not receive the whole string. Current mapping code at ApplicationsForPayment.jsx:195-197 DOES assign j.clientContact wholesale to base.clientName, so with a combined-contact string the concern will materialise. Consider splitting on em-dash/hyphen when populating afp-clientName and pushing the phone half into afp-clientPhone.
critical_code_review_comments: Rams.jsx:275 mount-effect: it runs once with [] deps. If the Resume click routes via /app/tool/rams (see GenericToolPage.jsx:250 redirect) the RedirectTo preserves ?draft=<id>, but if Rams.jsx mounts BEFORE the redirect completes on the Resume push, the effect fires with no id and never re-runs. Consider depending on `location.search` or using a dedicated router-driven trigger.

GenericToolPage.jsx effect race for session-recovery was fixed (recoveredFor ref merged into init effect) and the same class of fix is already applied for draft restore via draftRestoredFor ref — P1.5 passes because of it. Rams.jsx has a similar ref but a different failure mode (query param / toolId mismatch), NOT the same GenericToolPage race.

ApplicationsForPayment.jsx openEdit at line 202 does `{...emptyAfp(), ...a}` — this correctly preserves preparedSignature from the server response. P1.3 PASSED because backend PATCH round-trip retains preparedSignature and the spread does not blank it. Backend tests in iteration 40 confirm the PATCH shape.

ApplicationsForPayment.jsx pickProject/openNew at line 195: base.clientName = j.clientContact — no splitting on em-dash. If a Job carries a combined 'Name — Phone' clientContact, the whole string lands in afp-clientName. Add a split helper if this data shape is common.

rca of the issue: P1.4 RAMS RESUME FAIL — Rams.jsx has a dedicated draft-restore useEffect at line 275 with dependency array `[]`, guarded by a draftRestoredFor ref. It reads window.location.search via draftIdFromQuery() on mount. The observed symptom (all fields blank + no 'Draft restored' toast) means one of three early-returns hit: (a) `id` was null because draftIdFromQuery() ran before the query param was in the URL — this can happen if React StrictMode/router-navigation ordering places the mount before the searchParams apply; (b) `draftRestoredFor.current === id` was already truthy — unlikely on a fresh mount; (c) fetch returned a doc whose toolId !== 'rams' so the effect bailed out silently. Given DraftSaveButton.jsx line 34 serialises the draft under whatever tool.id it was passed (Rams.jsx passes {id:'rams',name:'RAMS'}), (c) shouldn't happen unless the /drafts list Resume link routes through a wrapper that rewrites toolId. Most likely cause is (a) or a router-provided location mismatch — the effect ran with an empty search string, returned early, and the RedirectTo path was already completed by the time state re-rendered. Recommend converting the mount effect to depend on `useLocation().search` (react-router) so it re-runs when the query param becomes available, plus a diagnostic console.warn on each early-return branch during dev.
